description:
Add a checked-in benchmark harness that records repeated timing runs as JSON artifacts at a stable repository path, so every published performance figure traces to an artifact instead of a single self-attested measurement.

## Background

Today every published timing is a lone, un-artifacted measurement. This task adds `scripts/benchmark-session-cost.sh`, modeled on the existing `scripts/benchmark-rust-build.sh`. The script builds the release binary, generates a fixture repository of a recorded issue count, and times each scenario with at least 3 warmup runs and at least 20 measured runs, emitting one JSON artifact at the stable path `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-<jit-commit>.json` — the jit commit in the filename so history accumulates. The committed `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json` is the first instance and the schema template the harness must reproduce.

Artifact schema (top-level keys): `schema_version`; `jit{version,commit,dirty,profile}`; `machine{cpu_model,logical_cpus,ram_kb,kernel,measurement_fs,repo_real_fs}`; `corpus{issue_count}`; `method{samples_per_command,warmup_runs,warm,cache_state,timing_clock}`; `commands[]{name,argv,class,n,min_ms,median_ms,p95_ms,max_ms,lock_files_created}`; and `mutation_syscall_summary{task_clock_ms,user_s,sys_s,page_faults,context_switches}`.

Scenarios in the `commands` array: baseline (`--version`), single read (`issue show`), read-all (`query available` and `issue list`), and single mutation (`issue update --priority`). The bulk-mutation scenario is intentionally excluded here; it is added later, once the bulk-update fix lands, so its numbers measure the fixed behavior.

Mutable scenarios need a reset protocol: the harness materializes a fresh fixture repository per measured sample (regenerate, or restore from a pristine copy) so no sample observes a prior sample's mutations; warmup runs use throwaway fixtures of the same shape.

Cache-state contract is warm-only: cold-cache measurement needs root to drop the page cache and is not assumed; warm means the page cache is primed by warmup runs against the pristine copy. Timings are comparable only across artifacts sharing the same `measurement_fs`.

Citation rule: every published timing must cite artifact path, command name, and stat (for example `session-cost-<commit>.json > issue_update_mutation > median_ms`); an uncited number is a staleness defect.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `scripts/benchmark-session-cost.sh` is checked in, builds the release binary, generates a fixture repository of a recorded issue count, and for each scenario runs at least 3 warmup and at least 20 measured runs, emitting one JSON artifact at `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-<jit-commit>.json`.
- [hard] REQ-02: The emitted artifact conforms to the schema of `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json`: the same top-level keys (`schema_version`, `jit`, `machine`, `corpus`, `method`, `commands`) and the same per-command stat fields (`name`, `argv`, `class`, `n`, `min_ms`, `median_ms`, `p95_ms`, `max_ms`, `lock_files_created`).
- [hard] REQ-03: The `commands` array covers the baseline (`--version`), single-read (`issue show`), read-all (`query available` and `issue list`), and single-mutation (`issue update --priority`) scenarios, and contains no bulk-mutation scenario.
- [hard] REQ-04: Each mutable scenario runs against a freshly materialized fixture per measured sample so no sample observes a prior sample's mutation, and warmup runs use throwaway fixtures of the same shape.
- [hard] REQ-05: The artifact records machine identity (cpu model, logical cpus, ram, kernel, measurement filesystem, real-repo filesystem) and a warm-only cache-state field.
- [hard] REQ-06: Any performance timing stated in repository prose or documentation cites artifact path, command name, and stat.

## Notes

Model the script structure on `scripts/benchmark-rust-build.sh`. Timing figures are machine-specific; record machine identity rather than asserting portability. Do not hardcode expected millisecond values in tests — the artifact is the contract, not any single number.
title: Benchmark harness and first session-cost artifact
